title: AES Key Collisions on the All-Zero Block
summary: When the AES key size exceeds the block size, collisions on the all-zero block must exist; finding distinct colliding keys in fewer than two to the sixty-fourth trials remains open.

formal_statement.body: When the AES key size exceeds the block size, distinct keys encrypting the all-zero block to the same ciphertext must exist. Determine whether two such keys, $k_1$ and $k_2$, satisfying $\operatorname{AES}_{k_1}(0)=\operatorname{AES}_{k_2}(0)$, can be found in fewer than $2^{64}$ trials; prior work on chosen-key settings or AES hashing modes does not resolve this specific problem.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of target-plaintext key collisions in AES.
assumptions: The AES key size exceeds the block size.
parameters: AES key size and block size: sizes whose ordering guarantees collision existence
k1 and k2: distinct AES keys sought in the collision search
The all-zero block: fixed plaintext encrypted under both keys
2^64 trials: strict upper work threshold for the desired search
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether two distinct AES keys that encrypt the all-zero block to the same ciphertext can be found in fewer than 2^64 trials.

citations.label: Key Collisions on AES and Its Applications

progress.summary: The paper quotes this as an explicit open problem, noting that prior chosen-key and AES hashing-mode work does not resolve it. Its reduced-round results leave the standard full-round question open.
citation_labels: Kodai Taiyama et al., Key Collisions on AES and Its Applications
